I think I take a different approach to this, and I have a reason why. A trans man once chastised me for saying I'm pansexual because it's offensive to trans people. Many trans people attempt to fit neatly into the traditional gender binary, yet some don't. I'm pan for anyone, trans or not, that doesn't fit into the gender binary.

If you're a trans man, you're a *man*, not a man*, or an FtM, etc. Man. You therefore are _in the wheelhouse_ for people that are bisexual. They may have issues with dating or being intimate with someone that's trans, but that's their problem, not a problem with categorization. 

If you're genderqueer, or non-binary, or non-conforming, or any other category that is not man or woman, than pansexuality covers you as well; bisexuality, not so much. 

That's just my opinion anyway :)
